questions.q: What is the exact gate sequence for the n=2 QFT circuit used in this lab?
options: H(q1), H(q2), H(q1), H(q2) with no controlled gates or swaps at all
Controlled-R2(control=q1, target=q2) followed immediately by a measurement
questions.explain: Following the general n-qubit construction with n=2: one Hadamard on q1, one controlled-R2 gate (n(n-1)/2 = 1 for n=2), one Hadamard on q2, and one swap (floor(2/2) = 1).

questions.q: In the hand-traced circuit applied to |1> = |q1=0, q2=1>, what happens at Step 2 (the controlled-R2 gate) and why?
options: The control fires because q2 = |1>, so the |1> component of q1 picks up a phase of i, while the |0> component of q1 is left unchanged
The control does not fire because q2 = |1> is considered 'off' in this convention
The gate has no effect in this trace because R2 is the identity matrix
Both components of q1 are multiplied by i regardless of q2's value
questions.explain: Controlled-R2 only applies R2 = diag(1, i) to the target (q1) when the control (q2) is |1>. Since q2 = |1> here, the control fires and the |1> component of q1 is phased by i.

questions.q: What is the final, exact result of hand-tracing the circuit applied to |1>, after converting back to index notation?
questions.explain: Tracing all four gate steps and converting the swapped basis states back to index notation gives 0.5|0> + 0.5i|1> - 0.5|2> - 0.5i|3>, matching the verified QFT|1> result from Lesson 6 exactly.

questions.q: When tracing the circuit applied to |2> = |q1=1, q2=0>, what happens at Step 2 (the controlled-R2 gate), and why does this matter?
options: The gate causes an error because R2 cannot act when the control is |0>
The circuit must be restarted from Step 1 whenever the control qubit is |0>
The control fires exactly as it did for |1>, applying a phase of i to q1's |1> component
The control does not fire, because q2 = |0> throughout -- so no phase is applied at that step, which is why the final result has no imaginary components at all
questions.explain: Since q2 = |0> throughout the |2> trace, the controlled-R2 gate's control never fires, so no complex phase i is ever introduced -- this is exactly why the final result 0.5|0> - 0.5|1> + 0.5|2> - 0.5|3> is purely real with alternating signs.

questions.q: Why does QFT|2> come out with amplitudes that strictly alternate +0.5, -0.5, +0.5, -0.5 with no imaginary parts, while QFT|1> has imaginary amplitudes?
options: Because j=2 is an even number and even numbers always produce real-only results in any Fourier transform
There is no real mathematical reason; it is simply a coincidence of the N=4 case
For j=2, the defining formula's phase is e^(2*pi*i*2k/4) = e^(pi*i*k) = (-1)^k, which is always exactly +1 or -1 (never off the real axis) because the exponent is always an integer multiple of pi
Because the controlled-R2 gate is defective and only works correctly for odd values of j
questions.explain: Plugging j=2 into e^(2*pi*i*jk/N) with N=4 gives e^(pi*i*k) = (-1)^k, which only ever takes the values +1 or -1 -- a structural consequence of j=2 being exactly half of N=4, not a coincidence.
